summary: Iter11 verification of 4 new backend features + regression against https://circles-demo-1.preview.emergentagent.com — 31/31 pytest cases GREEN. Feature 1 (private-circle rooms): POST /rooms with circle_id → 200 for owner; GET /circles/{id}/rooms members-only (non-member 403, unknown circle 404); GET /rooms filters private rooms for non-members (room absent) and keeps them for guide (room present); global rooms (no circle_id) remain visible/joinable/message-able to any authed user. Feature 2 (report from rooms): POST /reports {target_type:'room'|'message'} resolves circle_id from the room (verified in Mongo doc + visible via GET /circles/{id}/reports for the circle owner/mod); category:'csam' on a room → {priority:true} and shows up in GET /moderation/priority for guide (global moderator). Feature 3 (transparency): GET /moderation/transparency returns {generated_at, totals:{reports_received, reports_resolved, actions_taken}, months:[{month, received, resolved, actions_taken, by_category}]} — all counts non-negative, totals.reports_received >= sum of monthly received (last-6-month window); works for non-moderator (public transparency); unauth → 401/403. Feature 4 (account recovery): POST /auth/forgot-password returns {ok:true} for existing AND non-existent emails (no enumeration); POST /auth/reset-password with wrong code → 400 'Invalid or expired code'; HAPPY PATH — directly inserted bcrypt-hashed code into password_resets collection, reset-password returned access_token+user, new password logs in (200), old password rejected (401), re-using the same used code → 400; expired record → 400; forgot-password hits 429 after burst (3/min cap). Regression intact: guide+demo login, GET /feed, create post + like + comment in joined public circle, global-room join+send-message for non-member, event create+RSVP for member, self-gift 400, private-circle posts read 403 for non-member, under-13 register 403, serve_file traversal 404 (used %2E%2E encoding + non-APP_NAME namespace), DM IDOR 403.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 2257 lines — carried-over recommendation to split into routers (auth, circles, posts, rooms, events, conversations, wallet, moderation, compliance). Growth from 2017 → 2257 in this iteration is largely the four new endpoints.

transparency() loads up to 5,000 reports and 5,000 moderation_actions into memory on every request and buckets them in Python. Fine today, but with volume consider a Mongo $group aggregation keyed by `${substr: ['$created_at', 0, 7]}` and project totals + months server-side.

forgot-password sends the reset code via a best-effort email that swallows HTTPException from send_email() but does NOT swallow other exceptions. If send_email raises something non-HTTPException (e.g. a timeout from httpx or an SMTP-level TypeError), the whole handler 500s AND reveals that the account exists (because non-existent emails short-circuit before the try/except). Suggest widening the except to `Exception` or logging-and-swallow.

reset_password branches on `rec.expires_at < now_iso()` — comparing ISO strings works only because both strings are timezone-aware UTC and lexicographically ordered. If any legacy row was stored without the `+00:00` suffix the comparison will silently misbehave. Suggest parsing to datetime before comparing (or storing a Mongo Date).

create_report resolves circle_id but does NOT verify the reporter can actually read/access the target (e.g. a non-member can report a message in a private room they can't see — if they ever learn the message_id). Low-severity enumeration risk; consider gating target_id access.
assert_can_access_room() silently no-ops if room.circle_id is set but the circle is missing (orphan room) — pre-existing nit from iter10.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Base URL from EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL in /app/frontend/.env, all routes /api. Mongo at MONGO_URL in /app/backend/.env, DB_NAME=test_database (bcrypt v4 installed, pymongo 4.18 installed). Credentials: guide@circles.app/circles123 (owner of all seed circles + global moderator) and demo@circles.app/demo1234. Register MUST include date_of_birth (YYYY-MM-DD) + accepted_terms:true. Rate limits (slowapi in-memory, per-IP): login 10/min, register 5/min, forgot-password 3/min, reset-password 10/min. MUST run serially: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter11_features.py -n 0 -v` — pytest.ini addopts default to `-n 2 --dist loadscope` and this suite shares pytest module-level state (pytest.priv_room_id, pytest.global_room_id, pytest.priv_room_msg_id, pytest.csam_report_id) across classes which breaks across xdist workers. After running, wait ~60s before re-running so the forgot-password 3/min bucket drains. Reset-password happy path works by directly inserting a password_resets doc — bcrypt.hashpw(code.encode(), bcrypt.gensalt()).decode() is identical to the hash the app writes. The server's /files traversal check runs server-side on the DECODED path, so use %2E%2E (not literal ..) in tests because the `requests` library normalizes `..` segments out of the URL client-side. Email delivery via Emergent Resend is best-effort — forgot-password returns {ok:true} even if email fails; tests DO NOT depend on receiving an email. Agora/live-audio out of scope (/rtc-token returns 503).
rca_of_issue: N/A — zero backend bugs. Three transient failures on the first test run were test-script bugs (not product bugs) and were fixed in test_iter11_features.py: (a) assert j['user']['email'] compared to the raw TEST_<hex> email the test generated while the server lowercases emails on both register and login — fixed with case-insensitive compare; (b) forgot-password rate-limit test originally relied on exactly 2 prior calls being present in the 60s sliding window; replaced with a 5-call burst in-test that unconditionally proves 429 is reached; (c) /files traversal test used literal `../../etc/passwd` which the requests library collapses to `/etc/passwd` on the client, so the request never reached the server-side `..` check — fixed to use %2E%2E URL-encoding plus a non-APP_NAME-prefixed path. All four features behave exactly as specified.
